items.title: Health Guardian is live in the Google Health app on Pixel Watch 3/4/5 — Blood Pressure Trends, Insulin Resistance Trends and Sleep Breathing Quality; Fitbit Air later, behind Premium
items.text:
*HIGH* — Health Guardian is live in the Google Health app on Pixel Watch 3/4/5 — Blood Pressure Trends, Insulin Resistance Trends and Sleep Breathing Quality; Fitbit Air later, behind Premium
Update to the 2026-09-09 preview, on Google's new go-live post (2026-09-24). Owners of the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 can set the three features up now, free; the first monthly trend reports land in early October. Blood Pressure Trends estimates a monthly *trend* from pulse and motion, no cuff, with Google's own "not a replacement for a blood pressure monitor" disclaimer. Fitbit Air gets the BP and insulin trends "later this year" and only with Google Health Premium ($9.99/mo).
Where we stand: today's Google Health API v4 discovery document (rev 20260923, read directly) carries no data type for any of the three trends, so they exist only in the wearer's Google Health app, not on CardiTrack's data path. Google is now narrating a BP trend in plain language on the exact devices we integrate, which is a roadmap item of ours. blog.google is proxy-blocked from the sandbox: the post is as indexed and as corroborated by six same-day write-ups, not as read. Smallest next action: confirm the country list at source, and decide the caregiver copy for "the wearer's own app already shows a BP trend" within the DPIA's OI-2 limits.

items.title: Google Health API v4 discovery revision 20260923: self-sources data-source family with PERMISSION_DENIED semantics for write-only clients, value ranges on writes, and LF/HF spectral power on HRV points since rev 20260908
items.text:
*FYI* — Google Health API v4 discovery revision 20260923: a `self-sources` data-source family with `PERMISSION_DENIED` semantics for write-only clients, value ranges on writes, and (since rev 20260908) LF/HF spectral power on HRV points
The discovery document moved from rev 20260916 to 20260923 (read directly today; diffed against Google's published copies). New: a fourth `dataSourceFamilies/self-sources` on `reconcile`/`rollUp`/`dailyRollUp`, with a rule that callers holding only write scopes are restricted to it and get `PERMISSION_DENIED` on `all-sources`; explicit "Must be in the range" validation on write fields (HR 1–300, RMSSD 1–200, SpO2 0–100…). Not previously recorded from rev 20260908: `HeartRateVariability.metadata` now carries `lowFrequencyPower` / `highFrequencyPower`, and a `WebhookNotificationCloudLog` schema (a Cloud Logging record, not a payload change).
Unchanged and verified: 21 scopes, `PairedDevice`, `Subscription`/`Subscriber`, every endpoint we call, no `deprecated` flag. Where we stand: we request seven `.readonly` scopes and no `.writeonly`, and never pass a `dataSourceFamily`, so nothing bites. Next: run the field-population probe to see whether Fitbit/Pixel Watch HRV points now carry LF/HF, and decide whether frequency-domain HRV joins the SSA inputs.
https://health.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v4

items.title: Google Play: memory thresholds and a 25% DEX-optimisation floor enforced from February 2027; Zero-Tap Sign-In via the Restore Credentials API required from April 2027
items.text:
*FYI* — Google Play: memory thresholds and a 25% DEX-optimisation floor enforced from February 2027; "Zero-Tap Sign-In" via the Restore Credentials API required from April 2027
Android Developers blog, 2026-08-26 (read directly), not previously recorded. From Feb 2027 Play enforces dynamic-memory (anon RSS + swap), bitmap-memory and DEX-optimisation thresholds ("a minimum of 25% coverage across optimization, shrinking, and obfuscation"); from April 2027 any app with sign-in must restore the signed-in state on a new device through the Android Restore Credentials API. Non-compliant apps "may see reduced app visibility … and reduced publishing capabilities". Games exempt. The App Excellence guideline adds a "high-security" exemption naming healthcare and grandfathers Block Store integrations done by 2026-09-30 — whether that exemption applies to Play enforcement is unstated, and the Play Console help page is proxy-blocked.
Where we stand: Auth0 sign-in via the system browser, no Credential Manager or Block Store, so not grandfathered. Release builds already use R8 and CI uploads `mapping.txt`, so the DEX floor is probably met but unmeasured; the memory metrics have never been read. Next: read all three off Android vitals, then settle whether the healthcare exemption covers us or Restore Credentials needs a platform binding before April 2027.
https://developer.android.com/blog/posts/elevating-app-quality-reducing-memory-usage-and-improving-device-migration

items.title: FDA final order codifies cardiovascular machine learning-based notification software as Class II with special controls (21 CFR 870.2380, product code QXO)
items.text:
*FYI* — FDA final order codifies "cardiovascular machine learning-based notification software" as Class II with special controls (21 CFR 870.2380, product code QXO)
Federal Register 2026-18612, published and effective 2026-09-11 (eleven days before this window; new to the record). It writes the Viz HCM De Novo (DEN230003, 2023) into the CFR as a generic type: software that "employs machine learning techniques to suggest the likelihood of a cardiovascular disease or condition for further referral or diagnostic follow-up", identifying "a single condition" from "non-invasive physiological inputs obtained during routine medical care", "not intended to provide diagnostic quality output". Future entrants clear by 510(k) against it.
Why it matters: this is now the named US regulation for the one output our compliance docs say we must not produce — an ML "likelihood of a condition" about a person. The definition turns on medical-care inputs and single-condition inference, neither of which CardiTrack does, so wearable-trend narration without condition inference stays on the general-wellness side. federalregister.gov, govinfo.gov and accessdata.fda.gov are proxy-blocked: the identification text is as indexed, the special-controls list unread. Next: read §870.2380's special controls and cite it in `ai_act_classification.md` and the DPIA's OI-2 row, with the phrasings ("likelihood", "may indicate", any named condition) the MedGemma output guard must keep rejecting.
https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/11/2026-18612/medical-devices-cardiovascular-devices-classification-of-the-cardiovascular-machine-learning-based
